Set \(f'(x)=0\):
\[
-\frac{1}{3x^2}+\frac{3}{(1-x)^2}=0
\]
\[
\frac{3}{(1-x)^2}=\frac{1}{3x^2}
\]
\[
9x^2=(1-x)^2
\]
Since \(0<x<1\), take positive square roots:
\[
3x=1-x \implies x=\frac14
\]
Thus \(a=\frac14\), \(b=\frac34\). The minimum value is
\[
\frac{b}{3a}+\frac{3}{b}
= \frac{3/4}{3/4}+\frac{3}{3/4}
=1+4=5.
\]

\[
\boxed{5}
\]
